evidence.quote: A zero-field free-energy estimate does not by itself control the one-sided field derivative that defines spontaneous magnetization.

exclusions.query: Magnetization from a zero-field free-energy estimate alone
exclusions.reason: The field derivative requires uniform observable control before passing to pressure increments.

hypotheses.statement: For every fixed $S\in\{\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\ldots\}$ and every interaction satisfying [eq:interaction], $$\lim_{\beta\to\infty}\beta^{3/2}\bigl(S-m_{S,J}(\beta)\bigr) =\frac{\zeta(3/2)}{8\pi^{3/2}\sqrt{\det D_{S,J}}}. \label{eq:bloch-law}$$

For $E,T$ as above, $$\label{eq:pin-identities}
 d_E(i)=\frac{r(E,\{i\})}{1+r(E,\{i\})}\quad(i\notin E),
 \qquad
 \mathbb P_E(T\subseteq\mathcal B_E)\le(2r(E,T))^{m_T}.$$

For almost every exposure under $\mathbb P_P$ and every $i\in T$, $$\mathbb P_P(\mathcal R_i(E,T)\mid\mathscr H)=q_i(\mathbf a).$$ In particular, $$\label{eq:fresh-return}
                m_Tr(E,T)=\mathbb E_P\sum_{i\in T}q_i(\mathbf a).$$

Suppose $R\ge R_0$ and $t$ is regular for $z$ at radius $R$. Every nonnegative function $v$ on $\mathcal H_t$, supported on slots above $\mathfrak B_R(z)$, satisfies $$\label{eq:local-nash}
 \|v\|_2^{10/3}\le C\mathcal D_t(v)\|v\|_1^{4/3}.$$ The constant is independent of $R,z,t$ and the unavailable slots.

Let $R\ge R_0$, and let $(z_i)_{i=1}^m$ be a sparse list of centers, counting repetitions. At a fixed slice let $I\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,m\}$ be any subset for which the slice is regular for $z_i$ at radius $R$. For $i\in I$, let $\mu_i\ge0$ be a mass on the available slots, supported above $\mathfrak B_R(z_i)$ and with total mass at most one. For every finitely supported real $Y$, $$\label{eq:sparse-source-pairing}
 \left|\left\langle\sum_{i\in I}\mu_i,Y\right\rangle\right|^2
 \le C m R^\alpha\mathcal D_t(Y).$$

There are $\beta_0,c,C,\lambda>0$ such that, if $\beta\ge\beta_0$ and $\mathsf I(P)$ holds, then $$\label{eq:component-tail}
 \mathbb P_P\bigl(w\in\mathcal O_t^\gamma,
   \operatorname{rad}_w\mathcal C_t^\gamma(w)\ge h\bigr)
 \le C\exp(-ch^\lambda),\qquad h\ge1.$$ This holds for every deterministic time $t$, coset $\gamma$, and coordinate site $w$, with the same constants for all $\beta\ge\beta_0$.

Under $\mathsf I(P)$, for $\beta\ge\beta_0$, every deterministic time $t$, anchor $z\in\mathbb Z^3$, and radius $R\ge1$ satisfy $$\label{eq:irregularity}
 \mathbb P_P(t\text{ is not regular for }z\text{ at radius }R)
 \le\delta_R:=CR^3p^6+C\exp(-cR^\xi),
 \qquad \xi=\nu\lambda>0.$$

Let $E$ be allowed and let $T\ne\varnothing$ be a finite set of slot points at a deterministic cut $\theta$, disjoint from $E$. Put $P=E\cup T$, $m_T=|T|$, and $\eta=\mathbf 1_{T}$. At almost every exposure under $\mathbb P_P$, define $f=1$ on $T$; at every other cut hole let $f$ be the probability that the boundary-killed fresh walk ever hits $T$ at a subsequent integer turn. Then $0\le f\le1$, $f$ has zero boundary values, and, for $g=f-\eta$, $$\label{eq:hitting-energy}
 \sum_{i\in T}q_i(\mathbf a)
 \le m_T-\langle f,A_Qf\rangle
 =\langle\eta,Q\eta\rangle+2\langle Q\eta,g\rangle
       -\langle g,A_Qg\rangle.$$

With these definitions and zero extension to the available-slot graph at the split, $$\label{eq:suffix-energy}
 \int_I\mathcal D_{t_d(u)}(Y_d(u))\,du
 \le\frac12\bigl(\|y\|_2^2-\|U_d^*y\|_2^2\bigr)
 \le E_y.$$ Moreover $\|Y_d(u)\|_\infty\le\|y\|_\infty$.

For almost every exposure, define $$v=\sum_{n=1}^{K-1}Q^n\eta,\qquad y=g-v,\qquad
 E_y=\langle y,A_Qy\rangle,$$ with the empty sum interpreted as zero. Then $E_y\ge0$, $\|y\|_\infty\le K+1$, and the fresh return probability satisfies $$\label{eq:return-expansion}
 q_i\le\sum_{n=1}^{2K-1}\langle\eta,Q^n\eta\rangle
          +2\langle Q^K\eta,y\rangle-E_y .$$

For every fixed $K$, $$\label{eq:finite-word}
 \left|\mathbb E_P[(W_R(\mathbf d))_{ii}]
                 -(\widehat W_R(\mathbf d))_{ii}\right|
       =o_K(\beta^{-3/2}).$$ The error is uniform over $1\le n\le2K$, all direction words of length $n$, all cubes, deterministic cuts and slots, and all allowed pin sets $E$ with arbitrary finitely many extra pins. The product inside the expectation is formed before averaging over the exposure.

For every fixed $\beta>0$ and $h\ge0$, $$\lim_{N\to\infty}p_N^+(h)=p_\beta(h).
 \label{eq:boundary-pressure}$$

For $h\ge0$, the colored-picture law defining $Z^+_\Lambda(h)$ is a mixture of the zero-field pinned laws with pin sets $E=D_0\cup F$, where $F$ consists of time-zero slots. Under the mixing law, $$\Pr(i\in F)\le b(h):=1-e^{-\beta h}
 \qquad\text{for every time-zero slot }i.
 \label{eq:pin-marginal}$$ Moreover, $$S-(p_N^+)'(h)
   =\frac1V\sum_{i\in V_\Lambda}\mathbb E_F[d_{D_0\cup F}(i)].
 \label{eq:field-deficit}$$

evidence.quote: The uniform pin estimates, the finite-index geometric reduction, and the energy bound for a spread source are the reusable parts of the argument.

purpose: Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions

coverage.checked_domain: Exhaustive n=1..3, all nonempty pin subsets, zero to two transpositions, probabilities 0, 1/2, 1, identity final permutation; additionally all final permutations on three vertices with fixed probabilities 1/3 and 2/3.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact Fraction-weighted enumeration of every Bernoulli outcome; direct cycle tracing and next positive pin visits, without determinant or matrix inverse.
